global_rules: Every chart exposes source, vintage, unit, geography, accounting scope, and observed/estimate/forecast/scenario status.
Historical and modeled values have a visible seam and distinct line styles.
A scenario fan shows model spread; it is not converted into a probability interval.
Sparse publisher milestones are rendered as points or ranges. The application must not interpolate unless it visibly labels the interpolation as a dashboard transformation.
EV and data-center loads are overlays unless a chart uses a verified mutually exclusive decomposition.
Annual TWh charts do not claim peak capacity, reliability, or transmission requirements.
Tooltip precision may not exceed source precision; approximate and lower-bound values keep their semantic markers.

charts.title: U.S. electricity sales and use by sector, 1949-2025
charts.purpose: Show the observed evolution of residential, commercial, industrial, transportation, total sales, direct use, and total use.
charts.stack_rule: Only the four sector electricity_sales rows are stackable. Total sales, direct use, and total use are overlays or separate panels.
annotations: EV method break at 2023 applies only to EV overlay

charts.title: World electricity system demand, 2000-2025
charts.purpose: Show observed/estimated historical growth on Ember's gross-generation-plus-net-imports basis.
charts.scope_rule: Label as system demand = gross generation + net imports; not final consumption.
charts.prohibited: Connecting this line to IEA's 2030 final-consumption milestone without a visible scope break.

charts.title: U.S. generation-to-consumption balance, 2025-2050
charts.purpose: Compare power generation and consumption expectations without hiding direct use, imports, or the system residual.
charts.warning: AEO cases are conditional scenarios, not predictions.

charts.title: U.S. electricity-demand range across AEO2026 cases
charts.purpose: Show how 2050 demand differs across eleven internally consistent EIA cases.
charts.scenario_rule: Do not summarize the cases as a probabilistic confidence band.

charts.title: What consumes U.S. electricity by sector, 2025-2050
charts.purpose: Show residential, commercial, industrial, and transportation electricity sales across selected AEO cases.
charts.stack_rule: The four selected sales sectors are disjoint and may be stacked.
charts.annotation: Most on-road EV charging appears in residential/commercial sectors according to charging location.

charts.title: Residential electricity by end use, 2025-2050
charts.purpose: Explain heating, cooling, water heating, appliances, electronics, lighting, and other loads.
charts.stack_rule: Named physical end uses can be stacked; totals and accounting adjustment rows are excluded.
charts.overlay: ev_charging may be shown as a dashed overlay because its accounting relationship differs.

charts.title: Commercial electricity by end use, 2025-2050
charts.purpose: Explain cooling, ventilation, lighting, refrigeration, computing, server, and other loads.
charts.scope_rule: Data Center Servers is server compute only; related facility cooling/ventilation and other overhead are not isolated from broader end uses.
charts.prohibited: Labeling the AEO server row total data-center facility electricity.

charts.title: Data-center electricity: observed estimates and scenario range
charts.purpose: Show the scale and uncertainty of global and U.S. data-center demand.
charts.comparison_rule: Never connect total-facility and server-only points with one line.

charts.title: Electric-vehicle electricity demand
charts.purpose: Compare observed U.S. EV electricity, AEO charging-location scenarios, and global IEA milestones.
charts.us_scenario_transform: sum residential/ev_charging and commercial/ev_charging within each case/year
charts.accounting_rule: Overlay on total demand; do not add.
annotations: CPS and NZE 2035 milestones are lower bounds
AEO transportation sales excludes most location-assigned road charging

charts.title: Industrial purchased electricity by component
charts.purpose: Separate general industry, refining, and hydrogen-production electricity.
charts.stack_rule: The three components are disjoint. The total_purchased_electricity row is validation/overlay only.

charts.title: U.S. demand drivers indexed to 2025
charts.purpose: Compare economic activity, population, households, floorspace, vehicle sales, and travel without mixing native units.
charts.transform: index each scenario-variable to its own 2025 value
charts.tooltip: Show both index and native value/unit.
charts.warning: Co-movement does not establish a single-variable causal coefficient.

charts.title: Global electricity consumption by sector through 2050-2070
charts.purpose: Show multi-model conditional pathways for total final electricity and major sectors.
charts.hierarchy_rule: Never stack aggregate sectors with their subsectors.
charts.warning: The envelope is model spread, not probability.

charts.title: Electrification stress test for U.S. 2050
charts.purpose: Compare AEO2026 current-law cases with NREL EFS Reference, Medium, and High electrification endpoints.
charts.scope_rule: Label NREL EFS as a 2018/AEO2017-vintage scenario study and AEO2026 as a current-law conditional scenario family; do not splice their lines.
charts.purpose_note: The older EFS remains useful as an electrification stress test, not as a current forecast.

charts.title: Annual demand is not peak demand
charts.purpose: Teach why equal TWh can require different grid capacity depending on load shape.
charts.release_gate: Do not infer or fabricate hourly profiles from annual AEO data.

charts.title: Global electricity generation versus final consumption
charts.purpose: Compare matched NGFS secondary electricity generation and final electricity consumption through 2050-2070.
charts.scope_rule: The difference is a model-specific accounting gap that can include grid loss, own use, and other accounting effects; it is not technical transmission loss.
charts.warning: All values are conditional model scenarios, not observations or forecasts.
